approach: Add `check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request, attempt)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, with a `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request, attempt));` line right after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` in `refusing_check` (3119-3138). It applies when the reading has a capability and no question, the class is `code` or `tests`, at least one criterion is Behavior (the `check_code_survey` precondition, 3453), and the request, plus the retried job's request when `attempt` is set, is a wrong-output report. Round 5 fixes finding 1: the cue text is split into tokens in which `-` and `_` join characters into one token (`has_phrase`, 3293-3299, treats them as boundaries, so it is not used for cues). That makes `stale-reading`, `stale_build` and `wrong-SHA` single tokens, none of which is a cue. Error words (family i) now need an output noun or a copula on the same line and no creation or change word. `regression` followed by test, tests, guard or guards is not a cue. When the check applies, the reading needs (a) a criterion with `root cause`, a location token and a reason word, and (b) one Behavior criterion naming a test, a real-data word and a failure on the base. The error names each missing part with fixed phrases. Unit tests, corpus cases (retry and real-shape accept cases included), one READING_RULES line and one CHANGELOG entry follow. The reader prompt, pipeline, records and athena-cli are not touched.

decisions.choice: Tokenise each cue line (lowercase; split on every character that is not alphanumeric, `-`, `_` or `'`; trim `-`, `_` and `'` from token edges). Cue words must equal a whole token. Phrases (`no longer`, `is wrong`) are adjacent tokens. Do not use `has_phrase` for cues.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. `has_phrase` counts only alphanumerics as word characters (reading.rs:3297), so `stale` would match inside `stale-reading`, `stale_build` and `wrong-SHA`, which are real feature vocabulary (CHANGELOG.md 796, 1481, 3196; HISTORY.txt:574). With joined tokens none of them is a cue. `fixture` and `prefix` are also different tokens from `fix`.

rejected.why: Matches `stale` inside `stale-reading`, `stale_build`; `wrong` inside `wrong-sha`.
`fixture` and `prefix` contain `fix`.

decisions.choice: Decide applicability per line from three cue families, with no mandatory `Bug fix:` declaration. A line is a cue line only if it has no creation word (add, adds, create, creates, new, introduce, implement) and no change word (make, makes, change, changes, redesign, rename, refactor, migrate), except family (ii), which keeps no exemption. (i) error words: token wrong, incorrect, incorrectly, stale, broken, bug, bugs, regression, plus an output noun (page, output, report, listing, table, view, dashboard, site) on the same line or a copula (is, are, was, were, be, been, looks, seems) or content verb (list, lists, show, shows, display, displays) on the same line. The token `regression` is not an error word when the next token is test, tests, guard or guards. (ii) a token fix, fixes, fixed or fixing with an output noun on the same line, or with the token bug, bugs or regression (same regression exclusion). (iii) wanted content: a content verb (list, lists, show, shows, display, displays, include, includes, contain, contains, publish, publishes) with an output noun other than output and report, and either a strong restrictor (the token still or anymore, or the tokens no longer) or the token only on a line that starts with a content verb (after any bullet marker) or holds the token now.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: family (i) had no guard and fired on everyday feature vocabulary. Now `Add read-ahead and stale-reading re-check to the drain` (creation word, joined token), `Show stale_build in the status JSON` (joined token), `Add a regression test for the walk` (creation word, regression-test exclusion) and `Add a gate spec for a wrong-SHA push` are not cues. The class is also defined by requests that described wanted page content: HISTORY.txt:13 `Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page`; CHANGELOG.md:375 `now lists only proposals that wait for the owner`; CHANGELOG.md:384 `no longer lists proposals that were approved or rejected`. Each is matched by (iii). `Make the status page show only running jobs` is a feature change and is not matched. Known gaps, stated in the doc comment: a bug worded `The page should list only X` and a bug report such as `The walk is wrong` with no output noun, copula-free wording or fix word are not caught; a text floor cannot cover every wording, and the verifier and critic still judge each bug-fix job.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain `root cause` (a hyphen read as a space), a location token and the whole word because, why or since. A location token is `::`, `.rs`, `()`, an `_` with a letter on each side, or a `/` token with two or more slashes or a `.` extension. The doc comment says this is a text floor and the verifier and critic judge the diagnosis.

demonstrations.method: A unit test reads reading.rs with `include_str!("reading.rs")`. It checks the `refusing_check` body holds `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request, attempt))` after the `check_code_survey` step. It checks the doc comment before the definition holds `20261103-201526-t4qv`, `20261103-231808-3gkq`, `no diagnosis`, `base-failing real-data test` and the sentence `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.`
demonstrations.observes: The test passes, so the function exists, the step line follows the code survey step, and the doc comment names the cause and both jobs.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the function or the step line, or with a doc comment that omits the cause or a job, the assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Reads the source text with `include_str!`, in the style of the existing `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended` (reading.rs ~8197-8228, splits on `pub fn check_code_survey`). No production entry point is called and nothing is injected. The test is added by plan step 6. The string `pub fn check_root_cause_criterion` must not appear before the definition.

demonstrations.method: The corpus runs each case through `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (via `run(c)` in refusal_corpus.rs) with the case's request, reading, `attempt` and `repo_files()`. Refuse case `bug-fix-wanted-content-without-root-cause`: request `Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page.` plus dash bullets such as `The decisions page now lists only proposals that wait for the owner`, no error word; reading class `code`, a `Code survey:` assumption, a Behavior criterion, no root-cause criterion; expected `Refuse("check_root_cause_criterion")`. Its source says: rebuilt from the changelog and commit subject, the verbatim t4qv request is in records/. Accept case `bug-fix-reading-with-root-cause-and-real-data-test`: same request; the reading adds `The root cause is that decided proposals reach the page because list_proposals() reads every proposal and never excludes approved or rejected ones` and the Behavior criterion `Run cargo test: a test built from real approved and rejected decisions fails on the base tree and passes with the change`; expected Accept. Retry cases: request `try again on 20261030-060751-5389`, `attempt = Some(earlier(RETRIED_JOB, <the wanted-content request>))`, tags `retry-complaint` and `bug-fix-root-cause`; REFUSE `retry-of-bug-fix-without-root-cause`, ACCEPT `retry-of-bug-fix-with-root-cause-and-real-data-test`. Other refuse cases are in the input-form map in step 7.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` passes: each refuse case is first refused by `check_root_cause_criterion` and the accept cases are accepted. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` pass with the new step. These are case ids I planned; I did not run the test.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the refuse cases are accepted and the corpus reports `expected Refuse("check_root_cause_criterion")`; `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` also fails. If the check read `request` only, the retry refuse case is accepted and fails.

Guards: capability set, no question, class code or tests, a Behavior criterion, and a cue line in the request or attempt request. Fixture: a `Case` from the existing `case(..)` helper over `base_reading` (refusal_corpus.rs:106, 175), with `Case.attempt` (line 62) set to `earlier(..)` (line 202) for the retry cases; class, assumptions and criterion kinds set on the case after it is built. `repo_files()` holds `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` and `docs/guide.md`. demonstrations.method: Corpus accept cases and a unit test show the check leaves non-bug work alone. All have class `code`, a survey and a Behavior criterion unless noted. Corpus: `feature-page-that-lists-only-is-not-a-bug-fix` (`Add a page that shows only failed jobs`), `feature-change-make-page-show-only-is-not-a-bug-fix` (`Make the status page show only running jobs`), `feature-redesign-still-shows-is-not-a-bug-fix` (`Redesign the dashboard so it still shows the cost column`), `feature-stale-reading-recheck-is-not-a-bug-fix` (`Add read-ahead and stale-reading re-check to the drain`, from HISTORY.txt:574), `regression-test-is-not-a-bug-fix` (`Add a regression test for the walk`), `joined-tokens-are-not-cues` (`Show stale_build in the status JSON` and `Add a gate spec for a wrong-SHA push`), `cue-inside-a-longer-word-is-not-a-cue` (`Add a test fixture for the prefix parser`), `fix-without-an-output-noun-is-not-a-bug-report` (`Fix the directory crash`, `Retry on failure`), `steward-request-is-not-a-bug-report` (from `root_cause_request(&[])`, refusal_corpus.rs:214), `steward-cause-line-with-a-cue-word-is-not-a-cue` (the same plus `Cause: the planner chose the wrong file.`), `bug-fix-docs-reading-is-exempt`, `bug-fix-decline-is-exempt`, `bug-fix-reading-with-a-question-is-exempt`, `bug-fix-reading-without-behavior-criterion-is-exempt`. The unit test `root_cause_check_leaves_non_bug_work_alone` calls `check_root_cause_criterion` directly on the same shapes, on a class `design` reading with a cue request, and on a user request with a line starting `Introspection ` and no title line (the cue on that line still counts). The unit test `root_cause_cues_match_the_wanted_content_wording` also asserts positive cues: the three wanted-content lines, `The decisions page lists proposals that were rejected, which is wrong`, `The report is stale`, `Fix the bug where the walk skips files`.
demonstrations.observes: Every non-bug reading is accepted by the new check and every positive cue is refused. The existing unit and corpus tests that use `change the reading rules`, `add a greeting` and `root_cause_request` still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check ignored the class, the question, the decline, the Behavior precondition, the creation or change words or the steward template removal, treated `stale_build` or `stale-reading` as cues, or matched cues as substrings, the matching case would be refused by `check_root_cause_criterion` and the test would fail.

demonstrations.method: The unit test builds `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])` and replaces the criteria with one Behavior criterion that has neither a root cause nor a base-failing real-data test. It calls `check_root_cause_criterion(&reading, "The decisions page lists proposals that were rejected, which is wrong", None)` and asserts the error holds `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`. With a good root-cause criterion added, only the second phrase appears; with only a good test criterion, only the first. A Content criterion with real data, and the copied steward bullet, are each reported as missing. With request `try again on 20261030-060751-5389` and `Some(&attempt)` carrying the bug request the same error is returned; with `None` it is Ok. It also asserts `check_reading_text` returns `ReadingCheck::Refuse` with no newline and both phrases, which is what `athena check-reading` prints.
demonstrations.observes: Both phrases are in the error when both parts are missing; otherwise only the missing part's phrase appears.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check `unwrap_err` panics on an Ok result. A message naming only one part fails the two-phrase assertion.
